name: cfrfml_receive
prose: Static function cfrfml_receive(layr, pkt), receive path of the CAIF RFM layer; pkt is owned by this function. It takes rfml->sync (spin_lock) and releases it before returning, extracts one header byte (error: -EPROTO) and tests the segmentation bit. Segmented packet with no stored incomplete frame: a failed 6-byte header peek, or an erroneous pkt, gives -EPROTO; otherwise it records pdu_size from the header, stores pkt as rfml->incomplete_frm and returns 0 (nothing forwarded). Segmented packet with a stored frame: rfm_append extracts a 6-byte header (-EPROTO on failure or if it differs from the stored one) and appends pkt to the stored frame (-ENOMEM if that fails); if rfm_append returns NULL the error is returned, and if the appended packet is erroneous the function jumps out with err still 0, so it returns 0 without forwarding, without storing the new packet and without destroying anything. Otherwise the appended packet becomes rfml->incomplete_frm and it returns 0. Unsegmented packet: if a frame is stored, the same append is done as the last segment (with the same failure outcomes, including a return of 0 when the appended packet is erroneous), the stored pointer is cleared, and the assembled length is checked against pdu_size (mismatch gives -EPROTO). The packet (or reassembled packet) is then passed to the upper layer's receive, whose result is the error. On any non-zero err it destroys pkt, any appended packet and any stored incomplete frame, sets incomplete_frm to NULL, logs the error and calls layr->up->ctrlcmd with CAIF_CTRLCMD_REMOTE_SHUTDOWN_IND. After releasing the lock it converts -EAGAIN to -EIO and returns err.
note: All three reviewer claims right: segmented partial frames return 0 without forwarding (cfrfml.c:98-148 path with err = 0), and an erroneous appended packet returns 0 with no cleanup (rfm_append leaves *err = 0, cfrfml.c:124-129 and 153-157). Slice cut the head (function at 97).

name: j1939_ac_process
prose: Static function j1939_ac_process(priv, skb) handling a received J1939 address-claim frame; it returns nothing. It only logs and returns, without taking priv->lock, if skb->len is not 8, if the NAME in the payload is 0, or if the source address is not valid; it stores the NAME in skcb->addr.src_name first. Otherwise it takes priv->lock for writing (BH disabled) and looks up the ECU for the NAME (taking a reference). If that ECU exists and already has the claimed address, it drops the reference and releases the lock, without restarting a timer. If no ECU exists and the claimed address is unicast it creates one; if there is still no ECU (creation failed, or the address was not unicast) it releases the lock and returns. Otherwise it cancels the ECU's pending claim timer; if the claimed address is idle it unmaps the ECU, drops the reference and returns. Else it unmaps the ECU if its address was different and sets ecu->addr to the claimed address; then, if another ECU (prev) is currently mapped at that address: when this ECU's name is greater than prev's name it unmaps this ECU (prev keeps the address), otherwise it unmaps prev; in both cases the reference on prev is dropped; if this ECU did not lose, it starts the ECU claim timer. Finally the reference on the ECU is dropped and the lock is released.
note: Reviewer 1 right (timer not restarted when name and address already match; the contender with the smaller name keeps the address). Reviewer 2 right: the losing ECU is this one, and prev keeps its mapping (j1939 address-claim.c:229-233); the old prose swapped the two. Also added the case of no ECU with a non-unicast address.

name: j1939_sk_getsockopt
prose: Static function j1939_sk_getsockopt(sock, level, optname, optval, optlen). Without taking the socket lock it returns -EINVAL if level is not SOL_CAN_J1939, -EFAULT if get_user cannot read the int at optlen, and -EINVAL if that value (ulen) is negative. It then takes lock_sock and, for optname SO_J1939_PROMISC or SO_J1939_ERRQUEUE, sets the value to 1 or 0 from the socket's state bit; for SO_J1939_SEND_PRIO the value is j1939_prio(sk->sk_priority) (the mapped J1939 priority, not the raw socket priority); any other optname gives -ENOPROTOOPT with nothing copied. For the three known options it returns -EFAULT if ulen is smaller than sizeof(int), if put_user of the length to optlen fails, or if copy_to_user of the value to optval fails; otherwise it returns 0 after writing sizeof(int) to *optlen and the int value to optval. On the copy_to_user failure path *optlen has already been updated. The socket lock is released on every path after it was taken.
note: Reviewer 1 right (optlen already updated when copy_to_user fails, socket.c:808-811). Reviewer 2: already reflected in the packet text (no lock for the level / get_user / negative-length returns, 779-784). Reviewer 15 right: SO_J1939_SEND_PRIO uses j1939_prio(sk_priority) (795).

name: j1939_session_tx_dat
prose: Static function j1939_session_tx_dat(session) sending J1939 transport data packets. It fetches the queued skb covering byte offset session->pkt.tx * 7 with j1939_session_skb_get_by_offset and returns -ENOBUFS if there is none. It then sends packets while session->pkt.tx < pkt_end, where pkt_end is session->pkt.total for a non-ETP broadcast session and session->pkt.last otherwise. For each packet it computes the offset and length (at most 7 bytes). If offset + len exceeds the skb length it logs once and goes to out_free with -EOVERFLOW (skipping the rx-timeout step). A zero length sets -ENOBUFS and leaves the loop. Otherwise it calls j1939_tp_tx_dat; a negative result leaves the loop with that result (-ENOBUFS means the CAN queue was full; other errors are logged). On a successful send it sets session->last_txcmd to 0xff and increments session->pkt.tx and the done count; if pkt.tx is still below pkt.total and the packet delay (50 ms for broadcast, otherwise j1939_tp_packet_delay) is non-zero it schedules the tx timer with that delay and leaves the loop with result 0. After the loop, if at least one packet was sent it arms a 250 ms rx timeout, even when the loop ended with an error. The skb obtained at the start is released with kfree_skb when the result is non-zero and consume_skb when it is 0. The function returns 0 or the negative error above.
note: Prose matches j1939 transport.c:804-883. The reviewer's missing -EOVERFLOW and j1939_tp_tx_dat errors were already in the packet text. Added that the rx timeout is armed also on error exits via break.

name: j1939_session_tx_cts
prose: Static function j1939_session_tx_cts(session) sending a clear-to-send frame. It returns -ENOENT if j1939_sk_recv_match finds no receiver for session->skcb. Otherwise it computes len as the minimum of (session->pkt.total - session->pkt.rx), session->pkt.block and j1939_tp_block (255 if that is 0), and builds a CTS frame of 8 bytes (rest 0xff): for an ETP session the ETP CTS command with len and the 3-byte next packet number pkt.rx + 1, otherwise the TP CTS command with len and the 1-byte packet number pkt.rx + 1. If the command byte equals session->last_txcmd it returns 0 without sending anything. Otherwise it queues the frame with j1939_tp_tx_ctl (also when len is 0) and returns its negative error if that fails. On success it sets session->last_txcmd to the CTS command only if len is non-zero, arms a 1250 ms rx timeout and returns 0.
note: Prose matches transport.c:924-967; the reviewer's point (len 0 still sends, only last_txcmd is skipped) is already stated. Kept; tightened.

name: decode_bits
prose: Static function decode_bits(c), decoding one Ceph armor (base64) character: it returns 0..25 for 'A'..'Z', 26..51 for 'a'..'z', 52..61 for '0'..'9', 62 for '+', 63 for '/', 0 for '=', and -EINVAL (-22) for every other char value (including NUL and any non-ASCII value). It has no side effects.
note: Matches armor.c:20-35 (the contract's -22 clause already covers EINVAL; the earlier rejections concerned an older contract text).

name: prepare_sparse_read_cont
prose: Static function prepare_sparse_read_cont(con) of the ceph v2 messenger (a WARN_ON fires if in_state is not IN_S_PREPARE_SPARSE_DATA_CONT). If con->v2.in_iter is neither a bvec nor a kvec iterator it returns -EIO. For a bvec iterator it updates con->in_data_crc over the received bvec (from the bounce page, copying the data into the destination page, when the RXBOUNCE option is set), advances the cursor by in_bvec.bv_len and reduces cursor->sr_resid by that amount. If sr_resid is still non-zero it stages the next bvec truncated to sr_resid (into the bounce page with RXBOUNCE), reduces data_len_remain by its length and returns 0. If sr_resid reached 0 it falls through to the sparse_read step below. For a kvec iterator it updates in_data_crc over in_kvecs[0] only if in_kvec_cnt is non-zero and does not advance the cursor, then goes to the sparse_read step. Sparse-read step: it calls con->ops->sparse_read(con, cursor, &buf). A negative result is returned. 0 resets the kvecs, stages the plain-epilogue kvec of CEPH_EPILOGUE_PLAIN_LEN, sets in_state to IN_S_HANDLE_EPILOGUE and returns 0. A positive result with buf non-NULL resets the kvecs, stages buf as a kvec of that length, reduces data_len_remain by the result and returns 0. A positive result with buf NULL returns -EIO if it exceeds cursor->total_resid; otherwise it stages the next bvec truncated to sr_resid (with RXBOUNCE, allocating con->bounce_page if needed and returning -ENOMEM if that allocation fails), reduces data_len_remain by the result and returns the positive result.
note: Reviewer 15 right: after the last bvec of a sparse extent (sr_resid reaches 0) the code does not return but goes on to ops->sparse_read (messenger_v2.c:1930-1955), which the old text implied ended with 0. Reviewers 1 and 2 already reflected.

name: revoke_at_prepare_read_data_cont
prose: Static void function revoke_at_prepare_read_data_cont(con) of the ceph v2 messenger. It expects (each only checked with WARN_ON) that con_secure(con) is false, data_len(con->in_msg) is non-zero, con->v2.in_iter is a bvec iterator, and that resid = iov_iter_count(in_iter) satisfies 0 < resid <= con->v2.in_bvec.bv_len. It computes recved = in_bvec.bv_len - resid and, if recved is non-zero, advances con->v2.in_cursor by recved with ceph_msg_data_advance; after that advance it issues a WARN_ON if resid is greater than in_cursor.total_resid. It then subtracts resid from con->v2.in_iter.count, calls set_in_skip(con, in_cursor.total_resid + CEPH_EPILOGUE_PLAIN_LEN) and sets con->v2.in_state to IN_S_FINISH_SKIP. It returns nothing and takes no lock.
note: Reviewers 2 and 15 right: the only checks are WARN_ON(!resid || resid > bv_len) before the advance and WARN_ON(resid > total_resid) after it (messenger_v2.c:3684, 3690); there is no check of bv_len against total_resid. Reviewer 1 (data_len nonzero) is the WARN at 3681, already in the old text.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE3(sendmsg, int, fd, struct compat_msghdr __user *, msg, unsigned int, flags)
prose: Generated function __do_compat_sys_sendmsg(fd, msg, flags) (entry compat_sys_sendmsg). Its body returns the inline helper __compat_sys_sendmsg(fd, msg, flags), which returns __sys_sendmsg(fd, (struct user_msghdr __user *)msg, flags | MSG_CMSG_COMPAT, false). The result is whatever __sys_sendmsg returns (a byte count or a negative errno); this function itself takes no lock or reference.
note: Name changed to the macro head (net/compat.c:350). The call goes through the inline helper at compat.c:340-348; semantics as in the packet prose.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE4(sendmmsg, int, fd, struct compat_mmsghdr __user *, mmsg, unsigned int, vlen, unsigned int, flags)
prose: Generated function __do_compat_sys_sendmmsg(fd, mmsg, vlen, flags) (entry compat_sys_sendmmsg). Its body returns the inline helper __compat_sys_sendmmsg(fd, mmsg, vlen, flags), which returns __sys_sendmmsg(fd, (struct mmsghdr __user *)mmsg, vlen, flags | MSG_CMSG_COMPAT, false). The result is whatever __sys_sendmmsg returns; this function itself takes no lock or reference.
note: Name changed to the macro head (compat.c:364).

The result is whatever __sys_recvmsg returns; this function itself takes no lock or reference.

Its body returns __compat_sys_recvfrom(fd, buf, len, flags, NULL, NULL), i.e. __sys_recvfrom(fd, buf, len, flags | MSG_CMSG_COMPAT, NULL, NULL), so no source address is requested. The result is whatever __sys_recvfrom returns; this function itself takes no lock or reference.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE6(recvfrom, int, fd, void __user *, buf, compat_size_t, len, unsigned int, flags, struct sockaddr __user *, addr, int __user *, addrlen)

The result is whatever __sys_recvfrom returns; this function itself takes no lock or reference.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE5(recvmmsg_time64, int, fd, struct compat_mmsghdr __user *, mmsg, unsigned int, vlen, unsigned int, flags, struct __kernel_timespec __user *, timeout)

The result is whatever __sys_recvmmsg returns; this function itself takes no lock or reference.
note: Name changed to the macro head (compat.c:405-407).

The result is whatever __sys_recvmmsg returns; this function itself takes no lock or reference.

name: netif_set_alias
prose: Function netif_set_alias(dev, alias, len) in net/core/dev.c (the packet name dev_set_alias is the wrapper in dev_api.c; this code is its callee, and the slice held only its tail). It returns -EINVAL if len >= IFALIASZ. If len is non-zero it allocates a new struct dev_ifalias with kmalloc (-ENOMEM on failure) and copies len bytes of alias into it, NUL-terminated; if len is 0 the new alias is NULL. Under ifalias_mutex it replaces dev->ifalias with the new pointer (rcu_replace_pointer) and unlocks; the previous alias, if non-NULL, is freed with kfree_rcu. It returns len (the number of bytes set, 0 when clearing), not 0.
note: Name was wrong: the real function is netif_set_alias (dev.c:1531-1552); the caller does not allocate the alias, the function does, and it returns len on success (the doc comment on dev_set_alias in dev_api.c says 0, the code returns len). The old prose claimed the caller allocated new_alias.

name: netif_get_num_default_rss_queues
prose: Function netif_get_num_default_rss_queues() with no arguments; it may sleep, because it calls zalloc_cpumask_var(..., GFP_KERNEL), so it must be called from process context. It returns 1 if is_kdump_kernel() is true or if allocating the temporary cpumask fails. Otherwise it copies cpu_online_mask into the temporary mask, and for each CPU still in it increments a count and removes that CPU's topology_sibling_cpumask() from the mask (so it counts one CPU per sibling group, i.e. per physical core); it frees the mask and returns the count if it is 2 or less, else DIV_ROUND_UP(count, 2).
note: Reviewer 15 right: zalloc_cpumask_var(GFP_KERNEL) can sleep (dev.c:3366), so 'any context' was wrong. Reviewers 1 and 2 concerned the old formal contract (dropped).

name: netif_schedule_queue
prose: Function netif_schedule_queue(txq) returning nothing. It takes rcu_read_lock and holds it through the body. If netif_xmit_stopped(txq) is false it reads the queue's qdisc with rcu_dereference(txq->qdisc) and calls __netif_schedule on it; if the queue is stopped it does nothing. It then calls rcu_read_unlock. __netif_schedule sets __QDISC_STATE_SCHED with test_and_set_bit and, only if the bit was previously clear, queues the qdisc on the current CPU's output queue and raises NET_TX_SOFTIRQ; if the bit was already set it does nothing.
note: Reviewer 1 right (the RCU lock covers the __netif_schedule call, dev.c:3412-3418). Reviewer 15 right: __netif_schedule acts only if the SCHED bit was clear (dev.c:3394-3398).

name: bpf_convert_ctx_access
prose: Static function bpf_convert_ctx_access(type, si, insn_buf, prog, target_size), which emits eBPF instructions that translate an access to a field of the user-visible struct __sk_buff into the corresponding access on the kernel struct sk_buff; the packet slice is the middle of its switch and the name given there was a placeholder. It switches on si->off (there is no default arm), appends the instructions for the matching field to insn_buf through a pointer starting at insn_buf, and where the field is accessed with a narrowed width the bpf_target_off helper sets *target_size. Reads load into si->dst_reg from si->src_reg; for the writable fields (for example priority, mark, tc_index, cb, tstamp) a BPF_WRITE access emits a store instead. Some cases also set prog->cb_access or similar program flags. If si->off matches none of the cases, no instruction is emitted. It has a single return and returns the number of instructions written (insn - insn_buf).
note: Name was a placeholder; the real function is bpf_convert_ctx_access (filter.c:9720-10083), a single switch with no default and one return at its end. Old prose 'returns the number written, sets target_size' is correct but incomplete (no-match case emits nothing and returns 0).

name: netdev_debug_event
prose: Function netdev_debug_event(nb, event, ptr), a netdevice notifier callback that only asserts the locking expected for an event; nb is not used. It converts ptr to the net_device and switches on the event: NETDEV_XDP_FEAT_CHANGE asserts the device's netdev lock (netdev_assert_locked), then, like NETDEV_CHANGE, NETDEV_REGISTER and NETDEV_UP, asserts the ops lock (netdev_ops_assert_locked), then, like every other listed command, ASSERT_RTNL(); NETDEV_CHANGENAME instead asserts ASSERT_RTNL_NET(dev_net(dev)). It modifies no state, takes no lock and returns NOTIFY_DONE for every event.
note: Prose checked against lock_debug.c:12-73. Reviewer 2's omission (ops lock and RTNL for XDP_FEAT_CHANGE; RTNL for CHANGE/REGISTER/UP via fallthrough) is covered by the new wording.

name: mp_dmabuf_devmem_destroy
prose: Static inline stub of mp_dmabuf_devmem_destroy(pool) in net/core/mp_dmabuf_devmem.h for builds without CONFIG_NET_DEVMEM: an empty function that does nothing and returns nothing. With CONFIG_NET_DEVMEM the header only declares the function (implemented elsewhere), so this description covers the stub only.
note: Reviewer right: the old text described only the stub (header lines 21-33); scope now stated. Kept rather than dropped because the stub is a function.

name: __neigh_event_send
prose: Function __neigh_event_send(neigh, skb, immediate_ok); the caller must not hold neigh->lock, and skb may be NULL. It takes write_lock_bh(&neigh->lock). Returns 0 with skb untouched if the state has NUD_CONNECTED, NUD_DELAY or NUD_PROBE; if the neighbour is dead and its state has NUD_STALE; or after moving a live NUD_STALE entry to NUD_DELAY with a timer of DELAY_PROBE_TIME. Returns 1 and frees skb (kfree_skb_reason) if the neighbour is dead and its state lacks NUD_STALE. If the state is neither NUD_STALE nor NUD_INCOMPLETE: when MCAST_PROBES + APP_PROBES is non-zero it resets the probe count, sets NUD_INCOMPLETE, sets updated, and arms the timer at one jiffy later, or, when immediate_ok is true, at now + max(RETRANS_TIME, HZ/100) and sets immediate_probe; when both probe counts are zero it sets NUD_FAILED, unlocks, frees skb and returns 1. After that, if the state is NUD_INCOMPLETE (whether it just became so or already was) a non-NULL skb is queued on neigh->arp_queue, first dropping older queued skbs while the queued bytes plus skb->truesize exceed QUEUE_LEN_BYTES, and the result is 1 (also when skb is NULL). When the result is 0 or when the skb was queued the caller's ownership is as stated: on 0 the skb is untouched; on 1 it was queued or freed. On the normal exits it calls neigh_probe(neigh) when immediate_probe is set (which sends the solicitation and releases neigh->lock) and otherwise write_unlock, then local_bh_enable, and returns the result.
note: Prose checked against neighbour.c:1200-1285. Both reviewer points (dead-neighbour path, NUD_FAILED when no probes, rc 1 for INCOMPLETE even with skb NULL) are right and now stated. Added that with immediate_ok the timer is set to the retransmit time rather than one jiffy, and that an already-INCOMPLETE entry arms no new timer.

name: pktgen_if_write
prose: Function pktgen_if_write(file, user_buffer, count, offset), the write handler of a pktgen device file; it parses one 'keyword value' command from the user buffer and returns count on success. It returns -EINVAL (warning) if count < 1, and returns the negative error from count_trail_chars or strn_len if the leading whitespace or the keyword (at most 15 characters) cannot be parsed, -EFAULT if copying the keyword from user space fails, or the error from strndup_user (only when the global debug flag is set). It then matches the keyword and, for most keywords (for example min_pkt_size, pkt_size, delay, count, clone_skb, burst, flows, dst_min, dst_mac, vlan_p), reads its value with num_arg or copies a string with copy_from_user, returning that error if parsing or copying fails (-EFAULT for failed string copies), updates the corresponding pkt_dev field and writes an 'OK: ...' line into pkt_dev->result before returning count. Exceptions: some invalid values write an 'ERROR: ...' line (for example node, vlan_p, vlan_cfi) and still return count; imix_weights returns count without an OK line; debug sets the global debug variable; a vlan_id or svlan_id outside the valid range turns VLAN/SVLAN off and returns count without writing an OK or ERROR line; flag with an unknown flag name writes a flag list into the result and returns count. Specific error returns: rate and ratep return -EINVAL for a zero value; clone_skb returns -EOPNOTSUPP for a positive value in netif_receive mode or without IFF_TX_SKB_SHARING and -EINVAL for a positive value with IMIX entries or without F_SHARED; burst returns -EOPNOTSUPP or -EINVAL when unsupported; imix_weights returns -EINVAL when clone_skb is set; dst_mac and src_mac return -EINVAL when mac_pton fails; a flag change that is not allowed returns -EINVAL; xmit_mode returns -EOPNOTSUPP for an unsupported mode. If the keyword matches nothing, it writes 'No such parameter ...' into pkt_dev->result and returns -EINVAL.
note: Reviewer right: the vlan_id/svlan_id paths update fields but write no status line (pktgen.c:1706-1732), and imix_weights writes no OK line either; the old prose said an OK or ERROR line is always written. The old prose also omitted the 'No such parameter' -EINVAL return (1866-1867). Slice cut the head (function at 983).

name: pktgen_wait_all_threads_run
prose: Static function pktgen_wait_all_threads_run(pn). If try_module_get(THIS_MODULE) fails it returns 1 immediately without taking a lock or waiting. Otherwise it takes pktgen_thread_lock and, for each thread in pn->pktgen_threads in order, calls pktgen_wait_thread_run, which loops while the thread is running: it drops the mutex, sleeps interruptibly for 100 ms, re-takes it, and returns 0 if a signal is pending then, or 1 once the thread is no longer running (a signal that is pending when no sleep was needed is not noticed). The first thread that returns 0 ends the loop. If any thread returned 0 (a signal was seen), T_STOP is set in the control word of every thread in pn. It then releases the mutex and the module reference and returns 1 if every thread was waited for without a signal being seen, else 0.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the signal check is only inside the wait loop after msleep_interruptible (pktgen.c:3272-3283), so a pending signal with no running devices still gives 1. Reviewer 1 right: 1 is returned when try_module_get fails (3296-3297), without waiting.

name: sk_getsockopt
prose: Function sk_getsockopt(sk, level, optname, optval, optlen), the generic SOL_SOCKET getsockopt implementation (the slice was a middle fragment of it; the placeholder name was wrong). It reads the user-supplied length from optlen (-EFAULT if that copy fails, -EINVAL if it is negative), zeroes a union v, and switches on optname. Most options store an int in v.val, some store other sizes by setting lv (timestamping, timeouts via sock_get_timeout, SO_MAX_PACING_RATE, SO_COOKIE, SO_TXTIME, SO_NETNS_COOKIE). Specific returns inside the switch: -EOPNOTSUPP for some options on socket types that lack them (for example SO_PASSCRED, SO_PASSPIDFD, SO_PASSRIGHTS, SO_PASSSEC, SO_PEEK_OFF, SO_TXREHASH); -EINVAL for some options (for example SO_COOKIE or SO_NETNS_COOKIE when len is too small, and SO_PEERNAME); -ENODATA for SO_PEERPIDFD and SO_PEERGROUPS when no data is available; -ENOTCONN for SO_PEERNAME on an unconnected socket; -ERANGE for SO_PEERGROUPS when the buffer is too small (after copying the needed length to optlen); -EFAULT when copying to user space fails; the result of the helper for SO_BINDTODEVICE, SO_PEERSEC and SO_GET_FILTER and some variants; -ENOPROTOOPT for an unknown optname. For the ordinary int-like options it clamps len to lv, copies len bytes of v to optval (-EFAULT on failure), then at lenout copies len back to optlen (-EFAULT on failure) and returns 0. Some options (SO_PEERCRED, SO_PEERGROUPS, SO_PEERNAME, SO_GET_FILTER, SO_MEMINFO) do their own copy and jump to lenout, and SO_PEERPIDFD returns 0 itself. The socket is not modified, apart from taking a pidfd for SO_PEERPIDFD.
note: Name was a placeholder; the function is sk_getsockopt (sock.c:1716-2162). Old prose 'returns 0 or a negative errno without modifying the socket' lacked the specific returns; SO_PEERPIDFD creates a pidfd (a user-visible effect). I did not enumerate every option's value.

name: assign_proto_idx
prose: Static inline stub of assign_proto_idx(prot) used when CONFIG_PROC_FS is not set: it returns 0 and does not touch *prot. With CONFIG_PROC_FS a different definition of the same function sets prot->inuse_idx to the first free bit of proto_inuse_idx and returns -ENOSPC (after logging) if none is free, so this description covers the stub only.
note: Reviewer right: with CONFIG_PROC_FS the real function sets prot->inuse_idx and can return -ENOSPC (sock.c:4037-4048); the stub is the #else variant at 4056-4059, and scope is now stated.

name: release_proto_idx
prose: Static inline stub of release_proto_idx(prot) used when CONFIG_PROC_FS is not set: an empty function that does nothing and returns nothing. With CONFIG_PROC_FS the other definition clears the prot->inuse_idx bit in proto_inuse_idx when it is not PROTO_INUSE_NR, so this description covers the stub only.
note: Reviewer right: the CONFIG_PROC_FS variant clears the bit (sock.c:4050-4053); the stub is at 4061-4063 and scope is now stated.

name: devlink_nl_reload_actions_performed_snd
prose: Static function devlink_nl_reload_actions_performed_snd(devlink, actions_performed, cmd, info) sending a reply message for a reload. It allocates a netlink message with nlmsg_new (NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, GFP_KERNEL) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails. It then adds a generic netlink header for cmd with genlmsg_put (using info->snd_portid and snd_seq); if that fails it frees the message and returns -EMSGSIZE. It adds the devlink handle with devlink_nl_put_handle and a DEVLINK_ATTR_RELOAD_ACTIONS_PERFORMED bitfield32 attribute; if either fails it cancels the message, frees it and returns -EMSGSIZE. Otherwise it finishes the message and returns the result of genlmsg_reply(msg, info) (0 or a negative errno); the message is then owned by the netlink layer.
note: Reviewer (round 2) wrong: genlmsg_put failure goes to free_msg, which returns -EMSGSIZE, not -ENOMEM (devlink dev.c:498-500, 514-516); only the nlmsg_new failure gives -ENOMEM. Reviewer 1 right that -EMSGSIZE is returned on put failures; the old text already had it. Added the missing parameters.

name: dsa_tree_setup
prose: Static function dsa_tree_setup(dst) setting up a DSA switch tree. If dst->setup is already true it logs an error and returns -EEXIST without changing anything. Otherwise it calls dsa_tree_setup_routing_table; if that reports the tree as incomplete it returns 0 with dst->setup still false and nothing else done. Then it runs, in order, dsa_tree_setup_cpu_ports, dsa_tree_setup_switches, dsa_tree_setup_ports, dsa_tree_setup_conduit and dsa_tree_setup_lags. If a stage fails it tears down the stages that completed before it, in reverse order (conduit, ports, switches, cpu ports, routing table as applicable; a failure in the lags stage tears down conduit and everything before it, the lags stage itself is not torn down), leaves dst->setup false and returns that stage's error. If all stages succeed it sets dst->setup = true, logs, and returns 0.
note: Both reviewer points are right and already stated: the incomplete-tree case returns 0 with setup false and no stage run (dsa.c:880-882); a true dst->setup gives -EEXIST (874-878); the lags stage is not torn down on its own failure (900-902, 910-919). Slice cut the head (function at 869).

name: dsa_user_netdevice_event
prose: Static function dsa_user_netdevice_event(nb, event, ptr), a netdevice notifier callback; nb is unused and the device comes from ptr. By event: NETDEV_PRECHANGEUPPER: calls, in order, dsa_user_prechangeupper_sanity_check, dsa_conduit_prechangeupper_sanity_check, dsa_lag_conduit_prechangelower_sanity_check, dsa_bridge_prechangelower_sanity_check, dsa_user_prechangeupper and dsa_user_lag_prechangeupper, and returns the first result for which notifier_to_errno is non-zero; if none, falls out and returns NOTIFY_DONE. NETDEV_CHANGEUPPER: calls dsa_user_changeupper, dsa_user_lag_changeupper and dsa_conduit_changeupper in order, returning the first result with a non-zero notifier_to_errno; otherwise it returns NOTIFY_DONE (a plain NOTIFY_OK from a helper is not returned, because notifier_to_errno(NOTIFY_OK) is 0). NETDEV_CHANGELOWERSTATE: err starts at 0; if dev is a DSA user device it sets err to dsa_port_lag_change(its port, info->lower_state_info); then, if netdev_uses_dsa(dev), it overwrites err with dsa_port_lag_change(dev->dsa_ptr, ...) (so the first result is discarded in that case); it returns notifier_from_errno(err). NETDEV_CHANGE and NETDEV_UP: if netdev_uses_dsa(dev), it calls dsa_tree_conduit_oper_state_change with netif_oper_up(dev) and dsa_tree_conduit_admin_state_change with !qdisc_tx_is_noop(dev) and returns NOTIFY_OK; otherwise NOTIFY_DONE. NETDEV_GOING_DOWN: returns NOTIFY_DONE if dev does not use DSA; otherwise it marks the conduit administratively down, collects the tree's user ports whose cpu_dp is dev->dsa_ptr, closes them with netif_close_many(..., true) and returns NOTIFY_OK. Any other event returns NOTIFY_DONE. It takes no lock itself.
note: Reviewer 15 right: in the CHANGEUPPER case a successful dsa_conduit_changeupper does not make the function return NOTIFY_OK; the function returns only errors there and otherwise falls to NOTIFY_DONE (dsa user.c:3515-3531, 3615). Old text also said the first dsa_port_lag_change result is kept; the second call overwrites it (3540-3549). Slice cut the head (function at 3479).

name: flow_type_hashable
prose: Static function flow_type_hashable(flow_type): a switch that returns true for TCP_V4_FLOW, UDP_V4_FLOW, SCTP_V4_FLOW, AH_ESP_V4_FLOW, TCP_V6_FLOW, UDP_V6_FLOW, SCTP_V6_FLOW, AH_ESP_V6_FLOW, AH_V4_FLOW, ESP_V4_FLOW, AH_V6_FLOW, ESP_V6_FLOW (the values 1 through 12), and for IPV4_FLOW (16), IPV6_FLOW (17), ETHER_FLOW (18) and the GTP flows GTPU_V4_FLOW through GTPU_DL_V6_FLOW (19 through 30); it returns false for every other value, including 0, 13, 14, 15 and values above 30 (so the IPv4/IPv6 user flows are not hashable). It has no side effects.
note: All three reviewers' complaints right: ETHER_FLOW is 0x12 (18), not 0, and GTPU_DL_V6_FLOW is 0x1e (30) (uapi ethtool.h:2300-2363); the old prose and contract had the wrong ranges and wrongly included 0. Values checked against the enum.

name: flow_type_v6
prose: Static function flow_type_v6(flow_type): returns true for TCP_V6_FLOW (5), UDP_V6_FLOW (6), SCTP_V6_FLOW (7), AH_ESP_V6_FLOW (8), AH_V6_FLOW (11), ESP_V6_FLOW (12), IPV6_FLOW (17), GTPU_V6_FLOW (20), GTPC_V6_FLOW (22), GTPC_TEID_V6_FLOW (24), GTPU_EH_V6_FLOW (26), GTPU_UL_V6_FLOW (28) and GTPU_DL_V6_FLOW (30); false for every other value. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures result == (flow_type == 5 || flow_type == 6 || flow_type == 7 || flow_type == 8 || flow_type == 11 || flow_type == 12 || flow_type == 17 || flow_type == 20 || flow_type == 22 || flow_type == 24 || flow_type == 26 || flow_type == 28 || flow_type == 30); */
note: All three reviewers right: the GTP IPv6 flows are 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30 (GTPU_V6 0x14 ... GTPU_DL_V6 0x1e, uapi ethtool.h:2325-2363), not 19, 21, ... 29 as the old text said.

name: ethtool_mmsv_link_state_handle
prose: Function ethtool_mmsv_link_state_handle(mmsv, up), meant for task context with interrupts enabled. It first calls ethtool_mmsv_stop, which shuts the verify timer down synchronously (timer_shutdown_sync). Then, under mmsv->lock with interrupts saved: if up is true and mmsv->pmac_enabled is true, it calls configure_pmac(true) through the driver ops (when the op exists) and then ethtool_mmsv_apply. ethtool_mmsv_apply, when verify_enabled is false, calls configure_pmac(mmsv->pmac_enabled) and configure_tx(mmsv->tx_enabled); when verify_enabled is true it sets status to ETHTOOL_MM_VERIFY_STATUS_INITIAL, sets verify_retries to ETHTOOL_MM_MAX_VERIFY_RETRIES and, if the net device is running, calls ethtool_mmsv_verify_timer_arm, which re-sets up and arms the timer only if pmac_enabled, tx_enabled and verify_enabled are all true and status is neither FAILED nor SUCCEEDED. Otherwise (up false, or pmac not enabled) it sets status to ETHTOOL_MM_VERIFY_STATUS_INITIAL only if verify_enabled is true, and calls configure_pmac(false) and configure_tx(false) (when the ops exist). The lock is released before returning; it returns nothing.
note: Both reviewer points (status reset only when verify_enabled) are right and already in the packet text (mm.c:363-377, 417-425). Kept; added the stop semantics and the timer-arm condition location.

name: ethnl_tsinfo_start
prose: Function ethnl_tsinfo_start(cb), the start callback of a TSINFO_GET dump (the packet's placeholder name ethnl_tsinfo_dump_prep does not exist; the slice cut its head). cb->ctx is used as a struct ethnl_tsinfo_dump_ctx (BUILD_BUG_ON checks it fits). It allocates zeroed req_info and reply_data with kzalloc, returning -ENOMEM if either fails (freeing req_info when only the second failed). It parses the header attribute with ethnl_parse_header_dev_get(..., require_dev false); a negative result is returned after freeing both allocations. If the parsed request has ETHTOOL_FLAG_STATS it sets the extack message "stats not supported in dump", releases the header device reference with ethnl_parse_header_dev_put, frees both allocations and returns -EOPNOTSUPP. On success it stores req_info and reply_data in the context, sets pos_ifindex and pos_phyindex to 0, netdev_dump_done to false and pos_phcqualifier to HWTSTAMP_PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_PRECISE, and returns 0. In that case a device reference is held in req_info->base only if the header named a device (the dump may cover all devices when it does not); the matching release is ethnl_tsinfo_done.
note: Name was a placeholder: the function is ethnl_tsinfo_start (tsinfo.c:500-546). The old text said a netdev reference is always held on success, but ethnl_parse_header_dev_get is called with require_dev == false, so the device may be absent. Otherwise the old text matched the code.

name: hsr_get_node_data
prose: Function hsr_get_node_data(hsr, addr, addr_b, addr_b_ifindex, if1_age, if1_seq, if2_age, if2_seq); the slice held only its tail. It looks up the node by its A-address with find_node_by_addr_A(&hsr->node_db, addr) and returns -ENOENT, writing no outputs, if there is none. Otherwise it copies node->macaddress_B into addr_b, and for each of the two slave ports computes the age: *if1_age (slave A) or *if2_age (slave B) is INT_MAX if the node's time_in_stale flag for that port is set, or (when HZ <= MSEC_PER_SEC) if jiffies - time_in exceeds msecs_to_jiffies(INT_MAX), and otherwise jiffies_to_msecs of the difference. It stores node->seq_out[HSR_PT_SLAVE_B] in *if1_seq and node->seq_out[HSR_PT_SLAVE_A] in *if2_seq, and sets *addr_b_ifindex to the ifindex of hsr_port_get_hsr(hsr, node->addr_B_port)->dev when addr_B_port is not HSR_PT_NONE (the returned port pointer is dereferenced without a NULL check) and to -1 (as unsigned) when it is HSR_PT_NONE. It returns 0 in that case. It takes no lock and no reference.
note: Old prose said the function always returns 0 and took the node as an argument: wrong, the node is looked up by address and -ENOENT is returned when absent (hsr_framereg.c:756-758). Slice cut the head (function at 743).

name: ieee802154_hdr_addr_len
prose: Static function ieee802154_hdr_addr_len(mode, omit_pan): the length in bytes of an IEEE 802.15.4 address field. With pan_len = 0 if omit_pan else 2, it returns 0 for IEEE802154_ADDR_NONE (0), 2 + pan_len for IEEE802154_ADDR_SHORT (2), IEEE802154_ADDR_LEN (8) + pan_len for IEEE802154_ADDR_LONG (3), and -EINVAL (-22) for every other mode, including the reserved value 1. It has no side effects.
note: Matches header_ops.c:198-208 and af_ieee802154.h:18-25 (NONE 0, SHORT 2, LONG 3, ADDR_LEN 8); the contract already includes the -22 case, so the earlier mechanical rejections no longer apply.

name: SHOW_FMT(index, "%d", wpan_phy_idx)
prose: Generated sysfs attribute function index_show(dev, attr, buf) (from SHOW_FMT(index, "%d", wpan_phy_idx), which also defines the read-only attribute dev_attr_index). It converts dev to its cfg802154_registered_device with container_of (dev must be the embedded wpan_phy.dev of a live registered device), writes the device's wpan_phy_idx as a decimal int followed by a newline into buf with sprintf, and returns the sprintf result, the number of bytes written. buf must be large enough (a sysfs page); it has no other effect.
note: Name changed to the macro invocation that generates the function (sysfs.c:36); prose matches the macro definition at sysfs.c:26-33.

name: cipso_v4_validate
prose: Function cipso_v4_validate(skb, option) validating a CIPSO IP option; the caller has already checked that opt[1] is not larger than the buffer. It returns 0 (with *option left equal to the original option pointer) if the option is valid, or a non-zero byte offset into the option of the first problem, in which case *option is set to opt plus that offset. Offsets: 1 if opt[1] < 8; 2 if no DOI definition matches the big-endian DOI at opt[2..5] (cipso_v4_doi_search under rcu_read_lock). Then tags are scanned starting at offset CIPSO_V4_HDR_LEN (6), not 8. For each tag at offset opt_iter: opt_iter if its type is not in the DOI's tag list, if the tag has no length byte (opt_iter + 1 == opt_len), or if the type is not one of RBITMAP, ENUM, RANGE or LOCAL; opt_iter + 1 if tag_len exceeds opt_len - opt_iter or is below the type's minimum length (RBM, ENUM, RNG) or, for LOCAL, is not CIPSO_V4_TAG_LOC_BLEN; opt_iter + 3 if the level in tag[3] is invalid (ENUM and RANGE always, RBITMAP only when cipso_v4_rbm_strictvalid is set); opt_iter + 4 if the category data is invalid (same conditions, only when tag_len is larger than the minimum); for TAG_LOCAL, opt_iter if skb is NULL or skb->dev is not a loopback device. The RCU read lock is taken after the length check and released before returning.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the scan starts at CIPSO_V4_HDR_LEN (6), not 8 (cipso_ipv4.c:1571-1573); the old prose said 8. Slice cut the head (function at 1546); other offsets verified against 1559-1675.

name: cipso_v4_doi_remove
prose: Function cipso_v4_doi_remove(doi, audit_info) removing a CIPSO DOI definition; the slice held its tail. Under cipso_v4_doi_list_lock it searches for the DOI; if none exists it unlocks and sets the result to -ENOENT with the list and reference counts unchanged. Otherwise it unlinks the definition with list_del_rcu, unlocks, and calls cipso_v4_doi_putdef, which drops the list's reference and, if that was the last one, invalidates the CIPSO cache and frees the definition through call_rcu; the result is 0. In both cases it then starts an AUDIT_MAC_CIPSOV4_DEL audit record with netlbl_audit_start and, if the buffer was obtained, logs the DOI and whether the removal succeeded (res=1 or 0) before returning the result. The caller holds no lock or reference afterwards.
note: Prose matches cipso_ipv4.c:510-539 and cipso_v4_doi_putdef (577-587). Slice cut the head (function at 510). No reviewer claim beyond the mechanical name one.

name: fib_sync_down_dev
prose: Function fib_sync_down_dev(dev, event, force) marking nexthops on dev as down; the slice cut its head. event is expected to be NETDEV_CHANGE, NETDEV_DOWN or NETDEV_UNREGISTER (for other values the flags are not changed but the loop body still runs). It sets scope to RT_SCOPE_NOWHERE, or to -1 when force is true, and walks dev's nexthop hash list, doing BUG_ON(!fi->fib_nhs) for each entry and skipping an entry whose parent fib_info is the same as the previous one. For each distinct fib_info it counts dead nexthops: a nexthop already flagged RTNH_F_DEAD is counted dead and left unchanged; one that is not dead, whose device is dev and whose fib_nh_scope differs from scope, gets RTNH_F_LINKDOWN set (plus RTNH_F_DEAD for NETDEV_DOWN and NETDEV_UNREGISTER), has call_fib_nh_notifiers(..., FIB_EVENT_NH_DEL) called, and is counted dead. With CONFIG_IP_ROUTE_MULTIPATH, for NETDEV_UNREGISTER and a nexthop whose device is dev, the dead count is set to fib_nhs and scanning of that fib_info stops. If the dead count equals fib_nhs, the fib_info gets RTNH_F_LINKDOWN (plus RTNH_F_DEAD for DOWN and UNREGISTER) and ret is incremented. fib_rebalance is called for every processed fib_info. It returns ret, the number of fib_infos all of whose nexthops were dead, whether just marked or already dead.
note: Prose matches fib_semantics.c:1952-2016. Reviewer 1's point (already-dead nexthops are skipped) is already in the packet text; added that the stated event precondition is not enforced by the code.
